Udacity capstone using simulated Starbucks rewards-app data, with a related Streamlit prototype.

Understanding and predicting offer response

An offer-response study that moves from messy event data to model comparison and a prediction interface.

Python · pandas · scikit-learn · XGBoost · SHAP · Streamlit

The question

Which customer and offer signals help estimate whether someone will respond to an offer?

The work

  • Join customer profiles, offer metadata and interaction events.
  • Clean placeholder ages, missing values and inconsistent event fields.
  • Compare logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost, including a check for target leakage.
  • Add an interface for manual input and CSV-based predictions.

What the repository demonstrates

  • Published model comparison explicitly distinguishes the leaked random-forest result from the corrected experiment.
  • Companion Streamlit code supports single-customer and batch prediction flows.

What I learned

  • Treat unexpectedly strong model results as a reason to investigate leakage.

Project context

  • Educational simulated-data case; not commissioned work for Starbucks.
  • Metrics shown are repository outputs, not a new independent benchmark.
Source references

This is a curated local case study based on the public project repository, not a rerun of the original analysis.
